newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan stocks end fraction higher.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan stocks end fraction higher.

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks closed a fraction higher on Tuesday with most investors on the sidelines ahead of next month's key local government poll, which has already been marred by violence, brokers said.
The Colombo all share index closed one point higher at 618.1, with price gains outnumbering declines by 21 to 12.
"Most investors are taking a wait-and-see attitude," said Leslie Uduwavidane, manager of business development and marketing at Ceylinco Stock Brokers.
Foreign purchases amounted to 18,177,675 rupees and sales 17,618,250 rupees.
There was interest in Bogala Graphite because of growth propects after it reactivated two mines, brokers said.
Turnover was 24.4 million rupees supported by 356,200 Sampath Bank at 48.75 rupees and 68,500 Tea Smallholder Factories Ltd at 24 rupees.
"The market is unlikely to go up immediately," said Dimuthu Abeysekera, a trader at Allied Phillips Securities. "One reason could be (the March 21) election."
Brokers say investors fear there could be violence closer to the poll, marred by the killing of a ruling coalition lawmaker earlier this month.
